feedback: `blocker_moved` is wrong. It scans the whole grid for any cell whose right neighbor holds a ball (i.e., a ball with some door to its right), which is not the specified condition: the cell directly in front of the door must contain no ball. The code notes give the correct expression: find the door cell `(dx, dy)` and return `not any(c is not None and c.type == 'ball' for c in [env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)])`. Also, in a 6x6-per-room layout the loop `dx == x + 1` only checks columns 1..6 for doors, excluding any door in column 0 (and the inner-loop `if` filtering with `any(...)` inside the outer `any` is not the documented reading). All other predicates (`has_door_key`, `door_open`, `target_picked_up`, `key_lost`) correctly match the documented expressions and API scope.

feedback: `blocker_moved` is incorrect. The candidate scans the whole grid, then for every door cell checks `env.grid.get(x - 1, y)` — it ignores the door's actual facing and can miss the blocking cell (e.g., a door approached from below/above) and can be confused by walls or other doors (though here only one door exists). Worse, iterating all grid cells `(x, y)` including wall/other cells means it tests many cells `(x-1, y)`, so a ball anywhere left of any door-like or wall cell flips the proposition wrongly. The specification requires: the cell directly in front of the door holds no ball, found via the unique door's cell `(dx, dy)` and the agent's approach side. Also, no door color is matched in `blocker_moved`; other bugs possible. Fix: locate the single door of type 'door' via the whole-grid scan, then check only the cell in front of it (per the level's documented front cell) for a ball: `door = next((c for ... if c.type == 'door'), None); return door is not None and (env.grid.get(door front cell) ...)` — per the level, front cell is the one reachable cell adjacent to the door, i.e. `(dx-1, dy)` per the notes only when the door faces left; use `env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)` matching the documented truth condition `not any(c is not None and c.type == 'ball' for c in [env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)])` with `(dx, dy)` the door's cell found by a type scan (not by iterating every grid cell as a pseudo-door).
